subject.title: WhatsApp QR-unavailable/headless login needs phone-code fallback

question: Should WhatsApp phone-code login be exposed through a generic channel-auth CLI/SDK method, or should the fallback remain a WhatsApp-owned login surface?
rationale: The requested fix crosses a public CLI flag, plugin-facing channel auth contract, WhatsApp credential-state handling, and live Baileys behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent API shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept Generic Login Method After Proof
options.body: Keep a typed generic phone-number login method, but require QR compatibility, partial-credential cleanup, upgrade/session tests, and live WhatsApp pairing proof before merge.

options.title: Keep It WhatsApp-Owned
options.body: Rework the fallback so phone-code login stays local to the WhatsApp plugin and does not expand the generic channel-auth contract yet.

options.title: Pause Until Live Dependency Proof
options.body: Leave this issue open and wait for stronger Baileys phone-code proof before accepting a public OpenClaw entrypoint.

recommendation.title: Accept Generic Login Method After Proof
recommendation.body: Keep a typed generic phone-number login method, but require QR compatibility, partial-credential cleanup, upgrade/session tests, and live WhatsApp pairing proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties steipete to the channel/plugin SDK boundary and WhatsApp QR login path, making them the strongest owner for the API-shape decision.
